title: Research: offload the MTP draft head to an external device for prediction
outcome: implemented (research; conditional go for a second-GPU prototype)

phase0_economics.config: offload, kv nvfp4 32768, memory-ratio 0.90, 16k greedy decode

depth1_cache2600.detail: +96 MiB alloc failed, 86 MiB free, 23.33 GiB used -> MTP depth1 needs ~3.1-5 GiB extra device memory; does NOT fit at cache2600 even at 32k

phase0_economics.verdict: MTP depth1 fits at cache1400 but is 0.51x SLOWER than plain despite 72.5% acceptance -> speculation does not pay on this box.

root_cause: The MTP draft layer's routed experts are bf16 HOST banks (engine/mtp.py build_mtp_draft_banks) fetched over the SAME saturated PCIe 3.0 x16 link as the target's experts.
So a draft step adds draft-expert H2D traffic on top of the target verify rows' (gamma+1) expert traffic -> roughly doubles the bottleneck that dominates decode (04b: gather 63.6%).
The earlier lookup result (34: -11..-44%) and this MTP result agree: on a PCIe-bound offload box, any speculation that adds expert traffic loses.
why_the_idea_is_directionally_right: MTP's computed tokens are only ~72% accepted, but the cost is the DRAFT EXPERTS crossing PCIe, not the proposal transfer.
Putting the draft head on a SECOND device with its experts LOCAL to that device removes the draft-expert traffic from the 3090's link entirely.

The cross-device payload is tiny: GPU0 -> second device = inputs_embeds [T,H] + target_hidden [T,4H] (~T*5*H*2 bytes; T=gamma+1, H=2560 -> tens of KB/step); second device -> GPU0 = draft_hidden [T,H]. PCIe 2.0 x4 (~2 GB/s) is more than enough; sync round-trip is small vs ~40 ms/step.
Offloading the head also frees ~3-5 GiB on the 3090 (depth1 used +5.0 GiB at cache1400), which is exactly the 15b fit blocker at 220k.

cross_device_contract.gpu0: embed_tokens(draft_tokens)->[T,H]; target_hidden [T,4H]; apply shared lm_head to the returned draft hidden -> [T,V]; verifier/spec.verify_step stays on GPU0
cross_device_contract.second_device: run Qwen4ExpMTPHead.forward (project + draft decoder layer + attention KV + draft MoE) with the draft expert banks resident locally
open_problems: draft attention KV currently lives in GPU0's pool via draft_qsa_layer_ids (the draft batch 'reuses the step's reserved pages'); a second-device head needs its own draft KV (small, a few tokens) or a cross-device page handoff
the engine is single-device today (model + pools + caches on one CUDA device); needs a --mtp-gpu placement + stream/event sync + a second draft expert cache
CPU as the second device is unlikely: the draft decoder layer's attention is a Triton/CUDA path (no CPU attention fallback), and reading the draft banks from DDR4 (~44 GB/s) would cost ~100 ms/step

decision.go_no_go: conditional GO - only worth prototyping on a SECOND GPU (not CPU), and only if the target-verify-row cost alone still leaves a win
decision.cheapest_next_experiment: measure the target-side verify-row cost in isolation (MTP with the draft expert fetch removed / draft computed for free) to see whether the remaining verify cost is below the plain baseline; if not, no placement of the draft head can help
decision.hardware_caveat: a CMP 90HX at PCIe 2.0 x4 is fine for the tiny cross-device payload, but CMP compute/driver support on Linux and the unlock reliability are risks; a second RTX-class GPU is safer

limitations: One prompt/config per point; accept rate from the server's cumulative spec counter.
No second-GPU prototype was built; the contract above is the design, not a measurement.
